method: Built-in image_gen tool; generated original illustration plates, not patient images, scans, homologated equipment drawings or biomechanical models.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original high-resolution medical illustration plate for a professional motorsport neurotrauma research website.
Create an exquisite, anatomically careful medical editorial illustration with the depth, restraint, sculptural form and meticulous finish expected in a leading clinical review journal. This must be a fully rendered anatomical painting, not a flat vector icon, not a diagram made of simple blobs.
Composition: landscape 3:2, a clean midsagittal section of an adult human head and brain in true lateral orientation, face/anterior to the RIGHT, posterior to the LEFT. Center the head in the canvas with a modest clear margin, showing cranial vault and upper neck; avoid a large empty border. Pure very pale cool gray-white background (#f2f6f5). No words, labels, arrows, badges, ruler, panel letters, frame, logos or watermark; those will be added in code.
Anatomy: convincing natural human cranial proportions; thin layered scalp and cranial bone cut edge around the brain; richly modeled cerebral medial cortex with organic gyri and sulci, visible pale gray/white matter distinction, a coherent C-shaped corpus callosum arching above the ventricular space, central diencephalon beneath it, anatomically continuous midbrain, a ventrally bulging pons and tapering medulla continuing into the upper spinal cord. The cerebellum must be posterior to the brainstem and inferior to the posterior cerebrum, with fine folia and a subtle branching arbor vitae visible in section. Keep the space between pons and cerebellum anatomically plausible. No extra brainstems, floating structures or duplicated organs. Avoid emphasizing tiny structures whose position cannot be reliably drawn.
Rendering: refined hand-painted scientific cutaway with carefully controlled volume and subtle surface texture, soft upper-left light, ambient occlusion in cortical sulci, delicate highlights on the cranial cut edge, soft contact shadows. Natural warm ivory cortex and pale rose tissue, muted cool blue-gray bone, warm cream white matter; cerebellum subtly differentiated, no rainbow segmentation. Elegant restrained translucency only at the outer skin silhouette so brain structures remain sharply legible. The exposed anatomy should have real depth and organic complexity, not thick cartoon outlines or plastic spheres.
Integrity: normal educational anatomy, no injury, hemorrhage, lesion, tissue deformation, activation heatmap or diagnostic claim. Original composition; do not reproduce any existing published figure.

Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original high-resolution motorsport occupant-protection illustration plate for a serious engineering/medical publication.
Create a meticulously rendered, polished technical medical editorial illustration with sculptural depth, cutaway material sections and realistic human proportions, suitable for the art direction of a leading clinical/scientific review journal. This must be an advanced rendered illustration, not a flat vector stick figure.
Composition: landscape wide 3:2, a close lateral three-quarter cutaway of a generic modern open-wheel single-seater cockpit, front/anterior toward the RIGHT. Crop out most of the long nose and wheels; focus on the helmeted seated driver from head through knees and the surrounding cockpit. Entire helmet, halo, shoulders, restraint system, seat and visible survival-cell cut edge must fit comfortably in frame. Clean pale cool gray-white background (#f2f6f5); no racing scene. No words, labels, arrows, badges, logos, team livery, watermarks, dimension lines or invented telemetry; labels will be added in code.
Core structure: a dark graphite carbon-composite survival-cell tub visibly cut away on the near side, with convincing layered wall thickness and a clean machined cut edge. Show the interior molded seat, cockpit rim, side headrest padding and footwell volume. Carbon weave should be subtle and local, not visually noisy. A metallic titanium-looking halo arches around and above the exposed cockpit, with a coherent curved horseshoe hoop attached rearward behind the driver and ONE central forward support mounted ahead of the driver's head. Do not draw a windshield, a roll cage or extra halo pillars.
Occupant: one adult driver with natural proportions in a reclined single-seater racing posture, wearing a plain light ivory fire-resistant suit and full-face helmet, dark visor facing right. The head should be visibly inside the halo's protective envelope, with space above it. Shoulders and neck should connect anatomically; arms flexed naturally toward a steering wheel in front of the chest, hands wearing gloves. Show enough torso/hip/upper-leg form to read the reclined posture without an implausibly giant head or toy anatomy.
Equipment relationships: a clearly distinguishable frontal head restraint (FHR) yoke rests on the shoulders behind the neck, UNDER the shoulder harness straps. A short dark woven tether runs from a visible anchorage at the rear-side of the helmet to the restraint behind the shoulder. Shoulder straps follow the shoulders and FHR forward down the torso to a central pelvic buckle, with a visible lap belt. No strap through the throat, visor, head or arm. Use subtle desaturated teal for the shoulder straps and muted warm bronze for the visible tether connector, so the relationships can be seen without making this an installation guide. The device is NOT a neck collar and is NOT a strap across the neck.
Rendering: studio upper-left light, luminous but restrained helmet highlights, soft suit folds, convincing leather/foam headrest and seat texture, layered composite cut edges, titanium halo highlights, subtle ambient occlusion between body, harness, seat and tub. Highly controlled shading and realistic material differentiation. Avoid thick uniform outlines, faceted low-poly geometry, bloated volumes or flashy cinematic lighting.
Integrity: generic educational apparatus, not a specific homologated chassis or installation specification, not a crash reconstruction or deformation simulation. No injury or patient case. Entirely original artwork, not copied from a published figure.
